title: The shared edge has no owner row: gateway-bff, the Redis session and the App Gateway route
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Information Flow v5.pptx (slides 2, 3 and 10); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 2, 7, 8 and 10); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx (sheet Services)
section: Information Flow v5 slide 2 (how information reaches the Workbench) and slide 3 (integration patterns, row 'Direct entry')
description: Every screen read in the deck crosses the edge: browser, App Gateway, gateway-bff, then one owning service, with the session in Redis and a short-lived user JWT from ACE Common. The deck names no owner because it describes one module. The Ownership Map v1 has one row per service P1 to P10 and S1 to S9 and no row for gateway-bff, the Redis session or the App Gateway route, so the flows of source slides 2 and 3 cannot be given a service code as their owner.
evidence: Information Flow v5 slide 2: 'Recovery Workbench module: reads those views only; case, rules, decision log, document hub, partner portal' and 'People and partners write directly through the screens and the partner portal'; slide 3: 'Direct entry | Workbench screens and the partner portal | Everything the Workbench is the system of record for'. Architecture v5 slide 7: 'ACE PLATFORM - SAME AKS CLUSTER, APP GATEWAY AND DATABASE'; slide 10 steps 1 to 4 name gateway-bff and ACE Common sign-in; slide 20 lists 'gateway-bff - shared platform - Spring Cloud Gateway - Redis session'. Ownership Map v1 sheet Services: 19 data rows, none for the edge.
proposed: Assign the edge to the platform epic RWB-PLT-EDGE and to the composite-route contract story RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19), and add one row for gateway-bff, the Redis session and the App Gateway route to the Ownership Map before wave 0 closes.

title: O05, decisions and outcomes for model learning, has no path once the data lake is removed
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Information Flow v5.pptx (slides 2 and 6); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 8, 37 and 38); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP-17)
section: Information Flow v5 slide 6, row O05; slide 2, box 'Out of the Workbench'
description: O05 sends decisions and outcomes to COLLINS daily through the data lake for model learning, and slide 2 sends the same batch to Power BI and COLLINS. Architecture v5 removes the data lake (INT-19 and INT-20, ADR-018, DP-17) and gives rwb-reporting a read model built from events. O04, reporting, has that replacement in P9; O05, model learning, does not: no source names a service, an interface or a file that carries decisions and outcomes to COLLINS after the lake is removed.
evidence: Information Flow v5 slide 6: 'O05 | Decisions and outcomes for model learning | COLLINS | Daily batch to the data lake | Daily'; slide 2: 'Power BI and COLLINS: daily batch to the data lake'. Architecture v5 slide 37: 'Data lake and Power BI feed (INT-19/20) | Removed: reports from rwb-reporting'; slide 8: 'Data lake / Power BI - not connected (INT-19/20 removed)'. Rules R5.5 DP-17: 'Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data'.
proposed: Confirm with the model owner whether COLLINS needs decisions and outcomes at all after wave 1. If it does, name the path (P9 rwb-reporting read model, or an outbound file through P2 rwb-integration) and add the story; until then O05 is out of scope and the deck says so.

title: Two rows read the ACE table ace_batch_run, which ADR-010 does not allow
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Information Flow v5.pptx (slides 8 and 9); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql (31 views); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 11 and 29)
section: Information Flow v5 slide 8, row 'ACE refuses a feed'; slide 9, row 'Batch complete' and its note
description: The deck reads the ACE batch record twice: slide 8 reads the last complete business date from ace_batch_run and slide 9 says the Workbench build checks that ace_batch_run shows the source complete. ADR-010 and DP-05 allow one read path only, the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views, read by rwb-source-data, and the physical schema carries recovery.v_ace_batch_status for that data. The deck names the ACE table rather than the view and does not say which service raises AceDataLate and runs the check.
evidence: Information Flow v5 slide 8: 'ACE refuses a feed | Reads the last complete business date from ace_batch_run'; slide 9: 'Batch complete | ace_batch_run shows the source complete for the expected business date by its cut-off'. Physical Schema v6: 'CREATE VIEW recovery.v_ace_batch_status' among 30 recovery.v_ace_* views. Architecture v5 slide 11: 'SQL view ... 30 recovery.v_ace_* views (ADR-010) ... Never: any other service reading the views'; slide 29 keeps one read path. Rules R5.5 DP-05.
proposed: Read the batch record through recovery.v_ace_batch_status in P1 rwb-source-data only and name P1 as the service that raises AceDataLate. The wording of slides 8 and 9 stays as issued; the new fallback slide gives the view name and the owner.

title: The deck gives the interaction ledger to one module and names no reader
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Information Flow v5.pptx (slide 2); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R3 default rulings, DP-18); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slide 15)
section: Information Flow v5 slide 2, box 'ACE' (what the one module holds)
description: Slide 2 lists what the single module holds, case, rules, decision log, document hub and partner portal, and does not mention the interaction ledger. The ledger is in P1 rwb-source-data under the R3 default ruling and DP-18, and the deck names no service that reads it and no call type. Architecture v5 slide 15 gives P1 the ledger row but no reader list, so which of the 19 services read the ledger, and how, is not determined.
evidence: Information Flow v5 slide 2: 'Recovery Workbench module: reads those views only; case, rules, decision log, document hub, partner portal'. Rules R3 default rulings: 'Interaction ledger | P1 rwb-source-data'; R5.5 DP-18: 'Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling)'. Architecture v5 slide 15 P1 OUT: 'schema rwb_source_data (ACE view contract, extension tables, freshness, reconciliation)'.
proposed: Keep the ledger with P1 and list its readers in the P1 contract before the wave 1 contract freeze: contact history for P6 rwb-comms, the case timeline for P3 rwb-case and the collections history for S2 rwb-treatment.

title: The deck does not say whether a partner result is a partner record or a dated data product
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Information Flow v5.pptx (slide 5); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slide 17); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx (sheet Rulings)
section: Information Flow v5 slide 5, row I13
description: I13 says partner results are entered in the Workbench and reads them as data products DP06, DP07 and DP08. The partner portal is S9 rwb-partner on Architecture v5 slide 17; the dated DP06 to DP08 copies are P1's under the Ownership Map rulings. The one phrase 'Entered in the Workbench' covers both, so the owner of a court date, an enforcement step, an appraisal report or a sale result is not determined, and neither is the service that publishes PartnerResultSubmitted.
evidence: Information Flow v5 slide 5: 'I13 | Partner results: court dates, enforcement steps, appraisal reports, sale results | Partners | Partner portal in the Workbench, as entered | Entered in the Workbench; DP06, DP07, DP08'. Architecture v5 slide 17 S9: 'schema rwb_partner (panel, partner users, instructions, results, fees, scorecards)' and 'topic rwb.partner.events.v1: InstructionIssued, PartnerResultSubmitted'. Ownership Map v1 sheet Rulings, rows dp_treatment and dp_guarantee_claim: 'the dated DP04 copies stay with P1 as the data engine'.
proposed: Record the result as S9 rwb-partner's own row and event, and keep the dated DP06 to DP08 copies with P1 as read-only data products built from the S9 events.

title: Users and roles are read through iam_group, and ADR-010 allows only the 30 views
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Information Flow v5.pptx (slide 5); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 14 and 29); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql (recovery.v_ace_iam_group)
section: Information Flow v5 slide 5, row I16
description: I16 reads users and the roles they hold through ACE sign-in, with groups coming from ACE ingestion to iam_group. Under ADR-010 and DP-05 only rwb-source-data reads the recovery.v_ace_* views, and roles, scope, masking policy and the DoA table belong to P4 rwb-access as data. The deck gives neither the view reader nor the group-to-role owner, so the row cannot be assigned to one service.
evidence: Information Flow v5 slide 5: 'I16 | Users and the roles they hold | Entra ID and the bank IAM | ACE sign-in; groups through ACE ingestion to iam_group | v_ace_iam_group; DP14'. Architecture v5 slide 14 P4 OUT: 'schema rwb_access (Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, DoA table, access log)' and 'REST ACE Common: sign-in, group-to-role (Entra)'. Physical Schema v6: 'CREATE VIEW recovery.v_ace_iam_group'. Architecture v5 slide 29: only rwb-source-data reads the views.
proposed: P4 rwb-access owns roles, scope, masking and DoA; P1 rwb-source-data reads recovery.v_ace_iam_group and serves it through its contract; sign-in and group-to-role stay with ACE Common.

title: SMS and LINE dispatch stays open under DL30 while Architecture v5 gives the call to rwb-comms
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Information Flow v5.pptx (slides 6 and 11); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 7, 17 and 20)
section: Information Flow v5 slide 11, row 'Who builds SMS and LINE dispatch'; slide 6, row O03
description: The gaps table keeps the question open whether the Workbench builds SMS and LINE dispatch or uses a bank-wide service where one exists (DL30). Architecture v5 gives rwb-comms the call to the ACE Common notification path (SMS, LINE) and leaves the bank-wide service undecided, so the deck has both an open decision and an owner for the call but no statement of which wins for O03.
evidence: Information Flow v5 slide 11: 'Who builds SMS and LINE dispatch | A bank-wide service where one exists; the Workbench squads otherwise | DL30'. Architecture v5 slide 17 P6 OUT: 'REST ACE Common: notification path (SMS, LINE)'; slide 7: 'NSS SMS - LINE OA | via ACE notification path'; slide 20 every service: 'REST ACE Common audit and PII logging'.
proposed: P6 rwb-comms owns the call to the ACE Common notification path for O03 and builds its own dispatch only if the ACE team confirms that no bank-wide service exists; DL30 stays open until then.

title: The WIN notices file window JOB-10 has two owners and no single accountable service
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Information Flow v5.pptx (slide 6); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 17, 19 and 44); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx (sheet Jobs)
section: Information Flow v5 slide 6, row O02
description: O02 sends demand, recall and sale notices for registered mail to WIN as a daily file from the Workbench. Architecture v5 splits the work: rwb-comms writes the notice and rwb-integration delivers the file, and the job map writes the owner of JOB-10 as 'rwb-comms + integration'. No source says which of the two owns the Airflow file window and the retry after a failed acknowledgement, so the fallback row of source slide 8 has no single owner.
evidence: Information Flow v5 slide 6: 'O02 | Demand, recall and sale notices for registered mail | WIN | File from the Workbench | Daily'; slide 8: 'An outbound file is not acknowledged | Sends it again. After the third failure, raises a task to the owning team'. Architecture v5 slide 44: 'JOB-10 | WIN notices | 16:00 | rwb-comms + integration | Airflow file window + workers'; slide 17 P6: 'Integration: deliverFile (WIN letters)'; slide 16 P2: 'FILE WIN (registered mail): daily outbound file (INT-14)'. Ownership Map v1 sheet Jobs JOB-10: 'Temporal Schedule WIN notices in rwb-comms (Airflow file window; rwb-integration delivers the file)'.
proposed: P6 rwb-comms owns the notice and the JOB-10 Schedule; P2 rwb-integration owns the transport and the retry, and publishes FileDelivered or FileFailed to P6.

title: Kafka has two roles in the deck and only one of them is named
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Information Flow v5.pptx (slide 3); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 9, 11 and 21); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R4, R5.5 DP-09)
section: Information Flow v5 slide 3, table row 'Event'
description: Slide 3 names one Kafka use, PII Kafka for personal data access logging, and one event path, AceDataReady and AceDataLate. Under ADR-015 every service also publishes business events on its own topic and every service writes DecisionRecorded to the shared rwb.decision-record.v1. The row therefore describes a Kafka platform that carries two kinds of traffic with different ACLs, retention and personal-data rules, and names only one of them.
evidence: Information Flow v5 slide 3: 'Event | Kafka | PII Kafka for personal data access logging. ACE batch status reaches the Workbench as AceDataReady and AceDataLate'. Architecture v5 slide 21: 'Recovery gets its own business-event topics and access rules, separate from ACE's PII logging topics'; slide 9: 'topic per service rwb.<name>.events.v1, 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention, key caseId'; slide 11: 'Never: Personal data in events'. Rules R4: 19 topics plus the shared rwb.decision-record.v1; DP-09.
proposed: Describe both roles on the new slides: the ACE PII topics for logging, unchanged, and the 19 business topics plus the shared ledger topic with their own ACLs, retention and no personal data.
